links.targetTitle: Every Spark Root Edit must pass Spark Risk Council review be

title: The SRC veto is time-boxed: silence for seven days advances the proposal automatically
content:
The SRC has seven days from a new Root Edit proposal to post a conclusion and a stand-alone risk analysis (A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4.3.1). A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4.3.3 then supplies the default: "If no SRC conclusion or request for extension is posted within seven (7) days of submission, the Operational Facilitator will move the proposal to the Snapshot voting phase."

Two further constraints close the obvious workarounds. An extension requires the SRC to post "a public justification" and is granted "at the Operational Facilitator's discretion" (A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4.3.2) — the Council cannot extend itself. And a Failed SRC Review notice must be posted before the voting window opens, or before it closes if already open (A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4.4.3), so the block must be exercised in the open and on the clock.

Together these eliminate the pocket veto — the most common failure of any review gate, where a body kills proposals by never getting to them and never having to justify anything. In Spark, declining to review is equivalent to approving.

One qualification undercuts this. The automatic advance applies "**provided** the proposal is aligned with the Sky Core Atlas and the Spark Artifact," which hands the Operational Facilitator an alignment judgment of its own. The gate the SRC cannot hold silently, the Facilitator can — with no stated deadline, standard of review, or notice requirement attached.
description: With no conclusion or extension request posted, the Operational Facilitator moves the proposal to Snapshot — the Council can block but cannot stall, and cannot grant its own extension.
